questions.prompt: On an unbuffered channel, what does a send do until a receiver is ready?

options.text: It blocks — send and receive rendezvous together
It returns immediately and drops the value

questions.explanation: An unbuffered send blocks until a receiver is ready; the two operations happen together, synchronizing the goroutines.

questions.prompt: What do you get when you receive from a closed, drained channel?

options.text: The zero value and a false ok flag (v, ok := <-ch)
A blocking receive that never returns

questions.explanation: Receiving from a closed channel returns the zero value immediately with ok == false, and a `range` over it ends.

questions.prompt: What happens if you send on a closed channel?
questions.explanation: Sending on a closed channel panics — which is why only the sender should close, and only after its last send.

questions.prompt: A send or receive on a ____ channel blocks forever.
questions.explanation: A nil channel is never ready, so operations on it block forever; an accidental nil channel causes a hang.

questions.prompt: Which channel rules are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Only the sender should close a channel
A buffered send blocks only when the buffer is full
Receivers should close the channel when done

questions.explanation: The sender closes (once); double-close panics; buffered sends block only when full. Receivers never close.

questions.prompt: Match each channel idiom to its use.

pairs.right: Receive until the channel is closed
Signal that no more values will be sent

questions.explanation: range drains until close, close signals completion, and directional types document who sends and who receives.
